fullText: The 10,100th meeting of the Security Council is called to an order. The provisional agenda for this meeting is the situation in Cyprus. The agenda is adopted. Security Council will now begin its consideration for item two of the agenda, I wish to draw the attention of the Council members to the document S/2026/8, the report of the Secretary-General on United Nations operation in Cyprus, the document S/2026/9, the report of the Secretary-General on this mission of good offices in Cyprus. Members of the Council, have before them a document S/2026/50, the text of the draft resolution submitted by the United Kingdom of Great Britain and Northern Ireland. The Council is ready to proceed to the vote on the draft resolution before it. I shall like to inform the Council that the Presidency of the Council has met with representatives of the parties. We have confirmed that They maintained their well-known position vis-a-vis the item on the Council's agenda. On the basis of those meetings, with the consent of the members of the Council, the Presidency has drawn the conclusion that the Council can proceed to take a decision on the draft resolution before it. If I hear no objection, I shall put the draft resolution to a vote now. There being no objection, it is so decided. I shall put the draft resolution to vote now. Will those in favour of the draft resolution contained in document S/2026/50 please raise your hands. Those who abstain? against the result yes the result of the vote is as follows 13 votes in favor zero votes against two abstentions the draft resolution has been adopted as a resolution 2815 of 2026 There are no more names inscribed on the list of speakers. Before adjourning the meeting, this is the last scheduled meeting of the Council for the month of January, I would like to express this sincere appreciation of the delegation of Somalia to the members of the Security Council and to **** the Secretariat of the Council, for all the support they have given to us. Indeed, it has been a busy and eventful month, and one in which we relied on consensus on several important issues within our purview. We could not have done it alone and without the hard work, support and positive contributions of every delegation and the representatives of the Secretariat, including the technical support team, conference services officers, interpreters, translators, verbatim reporters and the security staff. As we end our presidency, I now speak on behalf of the Council in wishing the delegation of the United Kingdom good luck in the month of February. The meeting is adjourned.
